title: Pathway memory is more robust to edge perturbation, perhaps from selection

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pathway memory is more robust to edge perturbation, perhaps from selection

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The memory capacity of biological ODE pathway models degrades significantly less than that of random networks when edges are randomly deleted and added, perhaps because of evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The memory capability of biological models is also much more robust to edge perturbation than those of random networks, as indicated in Figure 7, perhaps due to evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “3. Discussion”. Scope: 35 BioModels pathway models versus random gene-circuit models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The differential degradation result is directly reproducible. The proposed selective cause is historical and is not discriminated from model complexity or curation effects.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeat matched edge-addition and deletion trajectories and compare memory degradation between biological and random models. This resolves robustness, while attributing it to evolutionary pressure requires alternative nulls or comparative selection evidence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Edge edits may not preserve valid biochemical kinetics.

Evolutionary attribution is confounded by construction differences.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data existence: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A robustness script is public, so the biological-versus-random degradation contrast can be rerun. The claim's causal clause, that the gap is perhaps due to evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments, is not identified by edge edits. The measurable half is the robustness difference alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Randomly delete and add edges in biological and random models, rescore memory, and compare the drop. A significantly smaller drop for the biological models would confirm the robustness contrast; a similar or larger drop would refute it. The same curves do not test evolutionary pressure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Greater robustness is compatible with curation bias as well as with selection.

Edge add and delete on an ODE needs a rule for new kinetic parameters, which can dominate the memory change.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.42
data adequacy: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.72
